pr_body:
Calling Init()/Update() and then Init()/Update() again gave a different result when using the same key and iv.
Cipher modes that were using ctx->num were not resetting this value, this includes OFB, CFB & CTR.
The fix is to reset this value during the ciphers einit() and dinit() methods.
Most ciphers go thru a generic method so one line fixes most cases.

issue_context.title: Re-initialising an EVP_CIPHER_CTX does not work as expected
comments: I think this is the underlying cause of #12377 (RNG fork-safety regression). We are re-seeding the RNG after a fork, but the new key/IV for the EVP_CIPHER_CTX we have put in place have not taken effect.

Given that I'm away on holiday from tomorrow, I think its unlikely I'm going to be able to take the analysis much further before I go.

@slontis - any chance you can take a look?

Are there currently a set of tests that are run on every cipher provider?  If so, there should be a test to prevent other providers from making this mistake.  If not, it would be a good thing to add a set of tests that every provider needs to pass. (Commenting as reporter of #12377)

> Are there currently a set of tests that are run on every cipher provider?

We have evp_test which runs a subset of its tests for all providers. @slontis is currently re-working it (#12236) to expand its coverage.

> Given that I'm away on holiday from tomorrow, I think its unlikely I'm going to be able to take the analysis much further before I go.
> 
> @slontis - any chance you can take a look?

Will do..

With your code it took about 5 minutes to find the culprit..
the ctx->num field is initially 0 and gets increased by 4 in the update..
If I reset this back to zero on the second update it gives the correct result.
I will have to see where this gets reset in 111.

> @mspncp can you try this out?

I tried it locally and it works. Created #12414 for a CI test.

For most ciphers this is true,
If it calls des_generatekey() then it will use a different random each time. which means the update will return a different value. You would have to figure out if it calls this function.

FWIW, unlike OpenSSL, BoringSSL creates the same output (which is 0 bytes) on both calls, which is the expected result if we expect the internal cipher state to be reset upon the second call to `EVP_EncryptInit_ex`.
it is probably related to ctx->bufsz not being cleared also..
so it is a bug I think..
OK. We can create a new issue. And engage in a patch-test cycle until I encounter no more bugs around ctx re-initialization with my fuzzer.

In my commit I discuss the ones that dont work with correct input.
Note that the test I do sets up keys and iv that are large enough to handle all cipher types..
